title: Parallax
description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

items.title: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West oil pipeline following drone attacks launched from Iraqi territory.
items.content_text: Saudi Arabia shut down the East-West oil pipeline on September 10, 2026, following drone strikes launched from Iraqi territory that caused material damage and casualties. While all sources confirm the physical attack and the resulting infrastructure shutdown, reporting differs on the perpetrators' identities. Middle Eastern outlets focus on Iraqi accountability and regional stability, whereas Russian reports emphasize the involvement of Houthi rebels or pro-Iranian groups within a broader framework of global energy security.

items.title: Events and ceremonies mark the 25th anniversary of the September 11 terrorist attacks.
items.content_text: Global media outlets are reporting on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, which resulted in nearly 3,000 deaths. While all regions acknowledge the core tragedy and its impact on international policy, coverage differs significantly in framing. Western outlets emphasize internal security debates and the personal experiences of survivors, whereas Middle Eastern sources focus on the long-term geopolitical consequences of the "war on terror" and the specific roles of American leadership.
